# Introduction

Agriculture plays an important role in India's economy. Agricultural commodity prices frequently fluctuate due to changes in production, supply, demand, weather conditions, transportation and international trade.

The project titled "Agriculture Commodity Price Forecasting" aims to analyse historical agricultural commodity prices and develop a data-driven system to forecast future national prices.

This project considers five agricultural commodities: Onion, Tomato, Wheat, Rice and Potato.

The analysis uses production quantity, mandi arrivals, weather information, import and export quantities, wholesale prices and retail prices.

The project also examines mandi-to-retail price transmission and identifies procurement and hedging implications for agribusiness buyers.

# Problem Statement

Agricultural commodity prices are highly volatile and depend on several economic and environmental factors.

Farmers, traders, retailers and agribusiness buyers face difficulties in making purchasing and selling decisions due to uncertainty in future market prices.

Traditional market analysis may not adequately capture the relationship between production, market arrivals, weather and international trade.

Therefore, this project aims to use descriptive analytics and machine learning techniques to analyse agricultural price movements and forecast national commodity prices for the next 30 days.

# Objectives of the Project

The main objectives are:

1. To analyse historical prices of five agricultural commodities.
2. To compare commodity prices across different states and mandis.
3. To study the relationship between production and market arrivals.
4. To examine the influence of weather on commodity prices.
5. To analyse import and export patterns.
6. To examine wholesale-to-retail price transmission.
7. To develop a 30-day national price forecasting model.
8. To provide procurement and hedging insights for agribusiness buyers.

# Dataset Description

The dataset contains agricultural market information for five commodities: Onion, Tomato, Wheat, Rice and Potato.

It includes information about different states, districts, agricultural markets, arrival dates, minimum prices, maximum prices, modal prices, production, mandi arrivals, retail prices, weather conditions, imports and exports.

The dataset will be used for descriptive statistical analysis, data visualization, correlation analysis and price forecasting.


# Data Import and Initial Inspection

```{r import-data}
library(tidyverse)
library(lubridate)

# Import agricultural dataset
agri_data <- read_csv(
  "C:/CNT05 Project/agricultural_commodity_price_dataset.csv",
  show_col_types = FALSE
)

# Display first six records
head(agri_data)

# Display dataset structure
str(agri_data)

# Display dataset dimensions
dim(agri_data)

# Display column names
colnames(agri_data)
```

# Data Cleaning and Preparation

```{r data-cleaning}
# Check missing values in each column
colSums(is.na(agri_data))

# Check duplicate records
sum(duplicated(agri_data))

# Check data types
sapply(agri_data, class)

# Check unique commodities
unique(agri_data$commodity)

# Check number of states and markets
n_distinct(agri_data$state)
n_distinct(agri_data$market)

# Convert categorical columns into factors
agri_data <- agri_data %>%
  mutate(
    commodity = as.factor(commodity),
    state = as.factor(state),
    district = as.factor(district),
    market = as.factor(market),
    season = as.factor(season)
  )

# Display cleaned dataset
glimpse(agri_data)
```

# Descriptive Statistics


```{r descriptive-statistics}
# Summary of numerical variables
summary(agri_data %>%
          select(min_price, max_price, modal_price,
                 retail_price, production, arrivals,
                 imports, exports, temperature, rainfall))

# Average modal price by commodity
commodity_summary <- agri_data %>%
  group_by(commodity) %>%
  summarise(
    Average_Price = mean(modal_price, na.rm = TRUE),
    Minimum_Price = min(modal_price, na.rm = TRUE),
    Maximum_Price = max(modal_price, na.rm = TRUE),
    Average_Retail_Price = mean(retail_price, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

commodity_summary
```

## Interpretation of Descriptive Statistics

The descriptive statistical analysis provides an overview of agricultural commodity prices and their related factors.

The average modal price across the dataset is ₹2,540 per quintal, while the average retail price is ₹32.72 per kilogram. The modal price ranges from ₹1,144 to ₹4,606 per quintal, indicating considerable variation in market prices.

Average production is approximately 178,326 tonnes, and average mandi arrivals are 444.2 tonnes. The average temperature is 26.84°C, while average rainfall is 72.25 mm.

Imports and exports also show considerable variation, suggesting differences in trade activity across observations.

These findings provide an initial understanding of price variation, agricultural supply, weather conditions and trade patterns. Further commodity-wise and time-series analysis is required to identify individual commodity trends and forecasting relationships.


# Commodity-wise Price Analysis

```{r commodity-price-chart}
# Calculate average modal price for each commodity
commodity_price <- agri_data %>%
  group_by(commodity) %>%
  summarise(
    average_price = mean(modal_price, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Display results
commodity_price

# Create bar chart
ggplot(commodity_price,
       aes(x = commodity, y = average_price)) +
  geom_col(fill = "steelblue") +
  geom_text(
    aes(label = round(average_price, 2)),
    vjust = -0.5
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Average Modal Price by Commodity",
    x = "Agricultural Commodity",
    y = "Average Modal Price (INR/Quintal)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

## Interpretation of Commodity-wise Price Analysis

The commodity-wise analysis shows that Rice has the highest average modal price at ₹3,258.10 per quintal, followed by Tomato at ₹2,748.39 and Wheat at ₹2,593.96. Onion has an average modal price of ₹2,313.54, while Potato has the lowest average at ₹1,788.04 per quintal.

These differences indicate that agricultural commodities have different market price levels. Rice and Tomato show relatively higher average prices, whereas Potato has a comparatively lower average price.

This analysis provides a useful baseline for understanding price differences among commodities. However, average prices alone do not explain seasonal fluctuations or future price movements.


# Monthly Price Trend Analysis

```{r monthly-price-trend}
# Calculate monthly average price
monthly_price <- agri_data %>%
  mutate(
    month_date = floor_date(arrival_date, unit = "month")
  ) %>%
  group_by(commodity, month_date) %>%
  summarise(
    average_price = mean(modal_price, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Display monthly results
print(monthly_price, n = 20)

# Plot monthly price trends
ggplot(monthly_price,
       aes(x = month_date,
           y = average_price,
           color = commodity)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.9) +
  geom_point(size = 1.5) +
  labs(
    title = "Monthly Agricultural Commodity Price Trends",
    x = "Month",
    y = "Average Modal Price (INR/Quintal)",
    color = "Commodity"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

# Seasonal Price Analysis

```{r seasonal-analysis}
# Calculate average price by commodity and season
seasonal_price <- agri_data %>%
  group_by(commodity, season) %>%
  summarise(
    average_price = mean(modal_price, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Display seasonal price table
print(seasonal_price, n = Inf)

# Create seasonal comparison chart
ggplot(seasonal_price,
       aes(x = season,
           y = average_price,
           fill = commodity)) +
  geom_col(position = "dodge") +
  labs(
    title = "Seasonal Price Comparison of Agricultural Commodities",
    x = "Season",
    y = "Average Modal Price (INR/Quintal)",
    fill = "Commodity"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

# State-wise Price Analysis

```{r state-analysis}
state_price <- agri_data %>%
  group_by(commodity, state) %>%
  summarise(
    average_price = mean(modal_price, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

print(state_price, n = Inf)

# State-wise price visualization
ggplot(state_price,
       aes(x = state,
           y = average_price,
           fill = commodity)) +
  geom_col(position = "dodge") +
  labs(
    title = "Average Commodity Prices Across States",
    x = "State",
    y = "Average Modal Price (INR/Quintal)",
    fill = "Commodity"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1)
  )
```

## Interpretation of Seasonal and State-wise Price Analysis

The seasonal analysis indicates that summer has the highest average modal prices for all five agricultural commodities: Onion, Potato, Rice, Tomato and Wheat. Post-monsoon has the lowest average prices across the same commodities.

The state-wise analysis shows geographical variation in commodity prices. Rajasthan records the highest average prices for all five commodities, whereas Karnataka records the lowest average prices in this dataset.

These variations may be associated with differences in supply, demand, production, transportation and seasonal conditions. Further analysis is required to determine the relationships between these factors and commodity prices.

The results highlight the importance of considering seasonal and geographical factors when developing agricultural commodity price forecasting models.

# Correlation Analysis

```{r correlation-analysis}

# Select numerical variables
correlation_data <- agri_data %>%
  select(
    modal_price,
    retail_price,
    production,
    arrivals,
    temperature,
    rainfall,
    imports,
    exports
  )

# Calculate correlation matrix
cor_matrix <- cor(
  correlation_data,
  use = "complete.obs",
  method = "pearson"
)

# Display correlation matrix
round(cor_matrix, 2)

# Convert correlation matrix into a data frame
library(reshape2)

cor_long <- melt(cor_matrix)

# Create correlation heatmap
ggplot(cor_long,
       aes(x = Var1, y = Var2, fill = value)) +
  geom_tile(color = "white") +
  geom_text(aes(label = round(value, 2)), size = 3) +
  scale_fill_gradient2(
    low = "blue",
    mid = "white",
    high = "red",
    midpoint = 0,
    limits = c(-1, 1)
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Correlation Heatmap of Agricultural Variables",
    x = "",
    y = "",
    fill = "Correlation"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1)
  )

```

## Interpretation of Correlation Analysis

The correlation analysis examines the linear relationships between agricultural commodity prices and selected influencing variables.

The strongest positive correlation is observed between modal price and retail price, with a coefficient of 0.96. Exports have a moderate positive correlation with modal price (0.46), while imports show a weak positive correlation (0.24).

Production (0.15) and temperature (0.10) have weak positive relationships with modal price. Arrivals (0.05) show almost no overall linear relationship, whereas rainfall (-0.08) has a very weak negative relationship.

These findings provide an initial understanding of the relationships between market prices and agricultural factors. However, correlation does not establish causation. Commodity-specific and time-series analysis is required before selecting variables for the forecasting model.

# Commodity-wise Correlation Analysis

```{r commodity-correlation}

commodity_correlation <- agri_data %>%
  group_by(commodity) %>%
  summarise(
    Price_Retail = cor(modal_price, retail_price,
                       use = "complete.obs"),
    Price_Production = cor(modal_price, production,
                           use = "complete.obs"),
    Price_Arrivals = cor(modal_price, arrivals,
                         use = "complete.obs"),
    Price_Temperature = cor(modal_price, temperature,
                            use = "complete.obs"),
    Price_Rainfall = cor(modal_price, rainfall,
                         use = "complete.obs"),
    Price_Imports = cor(modal_price, imports,
                        use = "complete.obs"),
    Price_Exports = cor(modal_price, exports,
                        use = "complete.obs"),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

print(commodity_correlation, n = Inf)
print(commodity_correlation, width = Inf)
```

# National Monthly Price Aggregation

```{r monthly-price}

weighted_avg <- function(price, arrivals) {
  valid <- !is.na(price) & !is.na(arrivals) &
           is.finite(price) & is.finite(arrivals) &
           arrivals > 0

  if (!any(valid)) {
    return(NA_real_)
  }

  weighted.mean(price[valid], arrivals[valid])
}

national_monthly <- agri_data %>%
  mutate(
    month_date = lubridate::floor_date(arrival_date, "month")
  ) %>%
  group_by(commodity, month_date) %>%
  summarise(
    national_modal_price = weighted_avg(modal_price, arrivals),

    national_retail_price = weighted_avg(retail_price, arrivals),

    total_arrivals = sum(arrivals, na.rm = TRUE),

    avg_production = mean(production, na.rm = TRUE),

    avg_temperature = mean(temperature, na.rm = TRUE),

    avg_rainfall = mean(rainfall, na.rm = TRUE),

    avg_imports = mean(imports, na.rm = TRUE),

    avg_exports = mean(exports, na.rm = TRUE),

    .groups = "drop"
  )

print(national_monthly, n = 20)
```

# National Monthly Price Trends

```{r national_monthly-price}

ggplot(national_monthly,
       aes(x = month_date,
           y = national_modal_price,
           color = commodity)) +

  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +

  geom_point(size = 1.2) +

  labs(
    title = "National Monthly Agricultural Commodity Price Trends",
    subtitle = "Arrivals-weighted modal prices, 2023–2025",
    x = "Month",
    y = "Price (₹ per quintal)",
    color = "Commodity"
  ) +

  theme_minimal()
```
